sanskrit_verse:
anutpannaprajāyās tu patiḥ preyād yadi striyāḥ
niyuktā gurubhir gacched devaraṃ putrakāmyayā
transliteration:
anutpanna-prajāyās tu patiḥ preyād yadi striyāḥ
niyuktā gurubhir gacched devaraṃ putrakāmayā
sph_interpretive_translation: If a woman without issue approaches her husband's brother by appointment of elders for the purpose of progeny, then it is lawful.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not personal desire
Causation in action originates from collective spiritual necessity
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by role and dharma-adhikara
Restoration logic ensures continuity of lineage-consciousness
Consciousness alignment supersedes individual will in sacred duty
supreme_court_application: In adjudication at the highest level, intent and authorization must align with Vedic continuity. The court must verify that the act was performed under guru-sanction for dharmic propagation, not personal gratification. Responsibility lies with the governing council, not the individuals involved.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramana is established through guru-sanction and lineage-purpose. Anupurvasah shows that such unions manifest only when prior conditions of spiritual necessity arise. Proportional responsibility rests on the appointing body. There is no punitive consequence as the act serves cosmic order.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion process: Confirm alignment of intention with Vedic continuity
Responsibility assumption protocol: Elders affirm collective sanction
Capacity restoration: Ensure parties are spiritually prepared for union
Integrity reintegration: Reaffirm roles within family and societal dharma
final_declaration: This law proceeds solely from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. Dharma stands restored. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
